sections.label: Pallavi
sections.ta:
கமலாலய கரை உறையும் கருணை பொழியும்
கயிலாயர் மனங்குளிரும் கஜமுகனே
sections.translit:
kamalAlaya karai uRaiyum karuNai pozhiyum
kayilAyar manangkuLirum gajamukanE
sections.en: The elephant-faced Lord Ganesha is seated on the banks of the Kamalalaya Tank (pond) at the Thiruvarur Temple. He is the beloved son of Lord Siva.

sections.label: Anupallavi
sections.ta:
உருகி வரும் அடியார் இருவினை களைந்தே
பெருகி வரும் அருளாலவர் வாழ்வில் மெருகு தரும்
sections.translit:
urugi varum adiyAr iruvinai kaLaindhE
perugi varum aruLAlavar vAzhvil merugu tharum
sections.en: You remove the sins of both the present and past lives of your devotees. You bless them with a radiant life and elevate their stature through your boundless compassion.

sections.label: Charanam
sections.ta:
மங்கியதோர் தங்கத்தே மண்ணும் மாசும்
தங்கியதால் தரக்குறைவென்று எவர் உரைப்பினும்
உப்பும் உவர் நீரும் இட்டு பொன்னொளி வீச
மட்டுரைத்து மதிப்பினை உயர்த்தி சட்டென மறைந்த
sections.translit:
mangiyadhOr thangatthE maNNum mAsum
thangiyadhAl tharakkuRAivendRu evar uraippinum
uppum uvar nIrum ittu ponnoLi vIsa
matturaitthu madhippinai uyartthi sattena maraindha
sections.en: Sundarar, a great devotee of Lord Siva, once received gold coins from the Lord. He dropped them into the river at Virudhachalam and later recovered them from the Kamalalaya Tank at Thiruvarur. Some people, including professional goldsmiths, considered the gold to be of inferior quality because it was coated with soil, dust, and river sludge. However, you cleansed the ornaments by rinsing them with salt and tamarind water, restoring their brilliance and increasing their worth. After helping your father’s ardent devotee and friend Sundarar, you suddenly disappeared from the scene.

notes: The anupallavi of this song refers to the Vinayagar seated near the Kamalalaya Tank in the Thyagaraja Swami Temple at Thiruvaiyaru.The charanam refers to Vinayaga assessing the quality of the gold that Sundarar received from Lord Siva as Pazhamalainathar in Vriddhakasi (also known as Vriddhachalam or Thirumudukundram). According to the legend, Sundarar was not comfortable carrying all the gold with him. Lord Siva instructed him to toss it into the Manimukha River and retrieve it later from the Kamalalaya Tank in Thiruvarur. Goldsmiths in both Vriddhachalam and Thiruvarur examined the gold. When the gold was recovered from the Kamalalaya Tank, its quality appeared inferior because it had accumulated deposits from the river and soil. It is said that Vinayagar filed or polished the gold to restore its original brilliance, thus earning his name. The Sthalapuranam of the Virudhachalam Temple corroborates the story of Sundarar receiving gold coins from Lord Siva, casting them into the river there, and reclaiming them in Thiruvarur. For details, see: Sundarar tosses gold coins in the river in Virudachalam Reference is made in the charanam of this song to the story of Matturaiththa (Matru Uraitha) Vinayagar temple/Thyagarajaswamy temple in Thiruvarur. Sthalapuranam of Thiruvarur Thyagaraja Swamy temple, and the legend associated with Matru Uraitha vinayagar shrine at Kamalalaya tank, lend further support to the story: Thiruvarur Temple Legends For another version of the story based on legends of Thyagaraja Swamy temple in Thiruvarur, see: Matruraittha Vinayagar Story Besides the sthalapuranams, see also Muthusamy Dikshitar’s Gowlai raga kriti, Sri Mahaganapathim Revathumam in: Sri Muthuswami Dikshitar Keertanaigal (Second Edition) By Kallidaikurichi Vainika Vidwan A. Sundaram Iyer, Assisted By: Kallidaikurichi Veena S. Venkatesan, Music Books Publishers P.B.No. 379, Mylapore, Chennai 600004 (1998,Page 270). ஶ்ரீமஹாகணபதி ரவதுமாம்with editor’s comment: இது திருவாரூர் மாத்துரைத்த பிள்ளையார் மீது பாடப்பட்ட ஷோடசகணபதி கீர்த்தனை. அனு பல்லவி: கமலாலயத்தின் கரையில் வசிப்பவர் சரணம்: திருவாரூரில் தங்கத்தை உரைகல்லில் மாத்துரைத்த விக்னராஜர். Yet another fascinating version of the Mattu Uraitha Pillaiyar story goes like this: Mattu Uraitha Pillaiyar is the presiding deity of the temple located on the banks of the Kamalalayam Tank, opposite the Thyagaraja Swamy Temple at Thiruvarur. During one of Sundarar’s pilgrimages to Keezhvelur, his wife requested that he buy her a new gold necklace. Lacking the means, Sundarar prayed to Akshaya Lingeswarar, the local deity, for assistance. In response, Lord Siva instructed him to go to a nearby kiln and collect five gold bricks. Sundarar gathered the dusty bricks, and to ensure their safety, Siva told him to place the bricks in the temple well at Keezhvelur, and retrieve them later from the Kamalalayam Tank in Thiruvarur. When Sundarar brought the gold bricks to the temple goldsmith, the goldsmith declared that they were of inferior quality. Distressed, Sundarar prayed to Thyagaraja Swamy that night. Lord Siva assured him that he would send his son Ganesha to assist him the following morning. As Sundarar walked to the goldsmith’s shop the next day, a young artisan named Muthanna Asari accompanied him. Upon arrival, Muthanna Asari took the bricks from Sundarar, rinsed them with salt water, then with tamarind water, and finally touched them gently. Miraculously, during the mattu uraithal (scraping) process, the bricks began to shine and were revealed to be pure, precious gold. Overjoyed, Sundarar looked around—only to find that the young artisan had vanished. He then realized that the one who had restored the brilliance of the gold was none other than Lord Ganesha, the divine son of Siva. For a reference to this story and to Muthuswami Dikshitar’s kriti “Sri Mahaganapathiravatu Maam” in Raga Gowlai, see the link below: Another version of Matruraiththa Vinayagar story
